written.myAnswer: Smog inhibits plant growth by reducing the amount of carbon dioxide absorbed during photosynthesis.
Particulate matter is released by burning fossil fuels and also enters the air through natural processes such as volcanic eruptions.
CO is more poisonous than CO₂.
When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur forms oxides of sulphur. These irritate the eyes, cause breathing difficulties and contribute to acid rain.
Although CO₂ makes up only about 0.04% of air, increased CO₂ levels enhance global warming. This can melt ice caps, warm oceans, raise sea levels and contribute to extreme weather.

Carbon dioxide contributes to global warming and its effects, including melting ice caps, rising sea levels and extreme weather. Carbon monoxide is poisonous because it prevents red blood cells from carrying oxygen. Nitrogen oxides and sulphur oxides can cause breathing problems and acid rain; nitrogen oxides can also damage vegetation. Hydrocarbons contribute to air pollution and can cause respiratory and lung diseases. Particulate matter irritates the eyes, causes breathing difficulties, dirties clothes and reduces visibility. Ozone can cause chest pain, coughing, throat irritation and congestion.

Major causes include vehicle and industrial emissions, crop burning and other combustion sources. In winter, smoke can mix with fog to form smog, while pollutants such as nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide, particulate matter and volatile organic compounds build up in the air.
